title.narrative: Output 5.2. Increased capacity of Member States to strengthen skills and lifelong learning policies, governance models and financing system

description.narrative: Between 2022 and 2023, the Ministry of Education - Directorate General for TVET established 30 School Advisory Boards (SAB) in public TVET schools and institutes by Ministerial decree with joint public and private sector memberships aiming to create better linkages between TVET and the industry and to ensure quality and relevance of TVET education and foster graduates’ employability. Additionally, the Ministry of Education adopted a new governance model in the form of Public Private Partnership Memorandum of Understanding to promote life-long learning and create better quality education and an enabling environment for a productive, innovative, and competitive industrial sector in support of a national recovery plan. With support from the Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation, the ILO is providing a capacity building programme for the well-functioning of School Advisory Boards in Lebanon, optimization of their performance, and designing result-based action plans. Between 2022 and 2023, the ILO facilitated the training of 59 members in partnership with ITCILO bringing the total number of trained members to 110 since 2021. The contribution of ILO to SABs is complemented by a Training of Trainers to 22 members in view of supporting the establishment of 120 new SABs. The training was coordinated, designed, and implemented in partnership with ITC ILO and in collaboration with Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ). The MoU was put in place by ILO in close consultation with the Association of Lebanese Industrialists, the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Industry with funding from the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation and the Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation.

Output 5.3. Increased capacity of Member States to design and deliver innovative, flexible and inclusive learning options, encompassing work-based learning and quality apprenticeships

description.narrative: By end of 2023, The Lebanese Authorities of TVET (Ministry of Education-DGTVET, Ministry of Agriculture, and Ministry of Labour) have applied ILO approach to Work Based Learning (WBL) in informal and non-formal TVET education and developed standard guidelines for implementation at national level In partnership with UNICEF, the ILO supported the Lebanese Authorities (Ministry of Education-DGTVET, Ministry of Agriculture) in developing a Work-Based Learning (WBL) manual building on ILO guidelines for quality apprenticeship and piloting the guidelines towards their adoption at national level. The manual was developed based on lessons learned and practices collected from pilots and capacity building programmes. The ILO trained 29 officers and practitioners on ILO standards tools to support adaptation to Lebanon context and contribute to the successful implementation of pilots and manual finalization. With funding from the Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation and the Kingdom of the Netherlands, the ILO piloted the manual in WBL programme in various occupations in agriculture, construction, green economy, agrifood processing and health sectors to impact the lives of 580 youth, women, adults, refugees, and persons with disabilities in vulnerable situations.

Output 5.1. Increased capacity of Member States to identify current skills mismatches and anticipate future skill needs

description.narrative: In 2022, the Lebanese Authority (Ministry of Labour – National Employment Office) assessed impact of the multiple crisis, including COVID19, on skills needs and skills gaps and identified labour market demand in three sectors including health, public infrastructure and printing and packaging using ILO tools. In 2023, the Association of Lebanese Industrialists identified skills needs and labour demand in the plastic sector in response to industrial and environmental change including the impact of COVID 19 using online skills needs assessment adapted from ILO tools. With support from UNICEF and in partnership with the Ministry of Labour - National Employment Office, the ILO developed a compiled report analysing skills needs for three sectors (health, public infrastructure, and printing and packaging) and policy recommendations to address challenges facing the labour market in Lebanon including TVET reform. With support from the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation, and in partnership with the Association of Lebanese Industrialists, the ILO introduced an online skills anticipation survey and piloted it in the plastic sector for the purpose of institutionalizing the process in the industrial sector. To anticipate skills needs and measure the impact of crisis and COVID 19, the ILO used as reference the European Training Foundation (ETF), European Centre for the development of vocational training (CEDEFOP), ILO guide and ILO guidelines on rapid assessment for reskilling and upskilling. The ILO also applied TREE method to deepen the understanding of informal sector skills needs and skills gaps in all seven governorates of the country.

title.narrative: 5.1.1. Number of Member States that have applied ILO approaches to measure skills mismatches and/or anticipate future skill needs at national and/or sectoral level
Output 5.3. Increased capacity of Member States to design and deliver innovative, flexible and inclusive learning options, encompassing work-based learning and quality apprenticeships

description.narrative: The Lebanese Authority (Ministry of Education – Directorate General of Technical and Vocational Education DETEVT), in partnership with the private sector, introduced a sustainable green education services to 6 technical schools in rural areas by installing solar power system as part of OJT training programme for 100 vulnerable youth and to prevent disruption of classes caused by the energy crisis for 4200 vulnerable students in these schools. Furthermore, the Ministry of Education-DGTVET integrated entrepreneurship in TVET education in 45 technical schools using ILO Know About Business (KAB) tools and trained more than 3000 students. The Lebanese Authority (Ministry of Agriculture) implemented 5 demand-driven inclusive skills programmes in the agriculture sector for 560 Lebanese and non-Lebanese (of which 45% women; and 44% youth (male and female)). With funding from the Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation and the Government of the Netherlands, the ILO provided technical and financial support to the Ministry of Education in sustaining technical education in rural areas as such the ILO supported the adaptation of curricula and implementation of the training on solar power system installation. Through this training, the ILO supported installation of solar power system. Furthermore, with funding from the Government of the Netherlands through the PROSPECTS programme in Lebanon, ILO collaborated with the Ministry of Agriculture (MoA) to develop CBT curricula and guided implementation of WBL programmes in 5 occupations in the agriculture sector where skills gaps were identified. Through this support, 26 teachers from the MOA Agriculture Training Schools (ATSs) were trained on at least one of the CBT curricula developed and contributed and facilitated the transition of 560 trainees to the labour market. With funding from the Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation, the ILO trained 63 teachers from DGTVE technical schools to support mainstreaming KAB education in TVET and facilitate smooth transitions of students to the labour market.
